title: Short-Term Institutions, Analyst Recommendations, and Mispricing: The Role of Higher-Order Beliefs

scopes.description: Author-supplied SAS data-construction workflow that creates the final dataset; it does not include the paper-wide regression/portfolio analysis programs.

requirements.description: Monthly CRSP input read as crsp.crspdata. The code expects cusip, permno, date, shrcd, prc, ret and shrout, and uses March/June/September/December rows in its turnover construction. A local monthly securities candidate has every expected field except SHRCD; a name-history join may supply it, but the code's author-shaped product, identifier history, quarter coverage and required construction history remain unverified.

routes.description: CRSP.MSF is a readable monthly-stock candidate with CUSIP, PERMNO, DATE, PRC, RET and SHROUT. It does not include SHRCD; catalog-listed CRSP.MSENAMES has SHRCD, PERMNO, CUSIP and validity dates, but an as-of join and author-compatible history have not been established.
routes.expected_period: Quarter-end months March, June, September and December; full required CRSP history and coverage remain unresolved.

requirements.description: Institutional 13F holdings input read as Holdings.Holdings_type. The code uses permno, rdate, mgrno, shares and cusip to create quarterly fund holdings. The frozen catalog lists the Thomson-Reuters S34 13F table as a product candidate, but its catalog fields do not show PERMNO and its one-row probe timed out; identifier linkage, reporting periods and coverage remain unverified.

routes.description: The frozen catalog identifies TFN.S34 as Thomson-Reuters 13F Holdings and lists manager number, report date, CUSIP and shares. A bounded one-row check timed out, so local readability and fields were not verified by the probe; the product needs a time-valid PERMNO linkage and author-compatible reporting history before it can supply Holdings_type.
routes.expected_period: Quarterly and semiannual holdings report dates mapped to quarter-end; exact covered history unresolved.

requirements.description: Prepared quarterly chars dataset merged into the final dataset. The comment identifies mcap, bmratio, io, avgdailyturnover, mom12, cusip, permno, siccd, qtrno2 and fyear; the later final filter also consumes prc. Its producer, history and schema are not supplied.
Prepared idioriskff dataset with qtrno2, permno and idioriskff, merged into finaldataset. Its producer, return/factor definition, identifiers and history are not supplied.

Prepared bushee_variables dataset with year, qtr, permno, io_tra and io; the code derives qtrno2 and transientpct=io_tra/io before merging by qtrno2 and permno. Its construction and mapping are not supplied.

Prepared fundturnover_ltstio dataset with year, qtr, permno, stio_fundturn and ltio_fundturn. The comment says these are calculated from fund turnover and institution holdings, but this source creates fundturnover_inst and stock_fundturnover, not fundturnover_ltstio.

IBES recommendation-summary input read as ibesrecosummary. The code uses cusip, statpers, meanrec and numrec, reverses the recommendation scale, and keeps the last statpers in each CUSIP-quarter; compatible IBES table, identifiers and history remain to be verified.

Prepared jointmz.earnvol input with cusip, fyear and earnvol. Its annual Compustat producer is absent. The appendix describes a five-fiscal-year standard deviation of deflated earnings with a minimum of three years. A readable North American annual-fundamentals candidate contains cusip, fyear, at and ib, but the producer, date coverage, earnings mapping and history remain unverified.

routes.description: COMP.FUNDA is a readable North American annual-fundamentals candidate with cusip, fyear, datadate, at and ib columns. It could be used to construct the prepared earnvol table if the omitted recipe, sample period and fiscal-year/CUSIP mapping are confirmed; the one-row sample does not establish nonmissing values or history.
routes.expected_period: Five fiscal years for the rolling construction, requiring at least three years; target-period bounds remain unspecified.

requirements.description: Prepared herdingmeasures_final2 input merged by qtrno2 and permno. The source does not state output measure names, construction, history or raw source mapping; no producer is supplied.

Prepared rddata input with rdsale, cusip and fyear. The producer, fiscal-year matching and ratio definition are not supplied. A readable COMP.FUNDA candidate contains cusip, fyear, xrd and sale columns, but those underlying fields do not verify the prepared ratio or its construction.

routes.description: COMP.FUNDA is a readable North American annual-fundamentals candidate with cusip, fyear, xrd and sale columns. A producer must establish the author's rdsale definition, units, fiscal-year mapping and sample history before this source can supply rddata.

It also consumes jointmz.earnvol without its stated annual Compustat producer. Source-level field names/keys are visible, but definitions, upstream order, histories and compatible inputs are not supplied. The datasheet's vendor/source inventory does not provide these producer programs or datasets.

The SAS source does not assign LIBNAMEs or define a working-directory/import setup for crsp, Holdings, jointmz or the unqualified prepared datasets. The frozen parser flags the three qualified datasets as dynamic. Required path and staging configuration remain unspecified.

SAS runtime availability is unverified because the frozen bounded startup probe failed to initialize TKELS. Do not infer absent licensing; runtime initialization must be resolved before a future authorized run.

The supplied source ends after filtering the SAS WORK table finaldataset and does not document a persistent output library, export format or downstream consumer. A durable output location/name can be configured during preparation; the remaining paper-wide analysis workflow is not supplied and is outside this data-construction target.

We have described the data collection procedure in the Section 3.1 of the paper and define all
variables in the appendix of the paper. The steps necessary to process the data are described in the
computer programs referred to in part 5 of this Data Description Sheet.

5. The computer programs or code used to convert the raw data into the final dataset used in the
analysis plus a brief description that enables other researchers to use this program. The purpose of
this requirement is to facilitate replication and to help other researchers understand in detail how
the raw data were processed, the final sample was formed, variables were defined, outliers were
treated, etc. This code or programming is in most circumstances not proprietary. However, we
recognize that some parts of the code or data generation process may be proprietary, including from
the authors’ perspective. Therefore, instead of the code or program, researchers can provide a
detailed step-by-step description of the code or the relevant parts of the code such that it enables
other researchers to arrive at the same final dataset used in the analysis. In such cases, the authors
should inform the editors upon initial submission, so that the editors can consider an exemption
from the code sharing requirement. Whenever feasible, authors should also provide the identifiers
(e.g., CIK, CUSIP) for their final sample. Authors should consult our FAQ Sheet on the JAR website for
further details.
Computer programs to convert the raw data into the dataset used in the analysis and a brief
description that enables other researchers to use this program are provided in the file
CPS_finaldataset_code.sas. Identifier (CUSIPs) of firms in the final sample are provided in the file

evidence.description: Datasheet says the program converts raw data into the final dataset, names CPS_finaldataset_code.sas, and identifies the supplied file as final-sample CUSIPs.
Step 1 names 13F holdings and specifies the monthly CRSP fields and filters used for the turnover construction.
The SAS program directly reads crsp.crspdata again to produce quarter-indexed CRSP prices.
The SAS program reads Holdings.Holdings_type and constructs a quarter-end date from rdate.
The program derives institution-level quarterly turnover from held shares and CRSP price, then computes the quarterly fundturnover measure.
The program weights institution turnover by shares and creates the stock-quarter fundturnlen measure.
The program describes chars as a quarterly prepared characteristics file, then merges it with the generated stock fund-turnover output.
The program reads idioriskff and left-merges it by qtrno2 and permno.
The program reads bushee_variables, constructs qtrno2 and transientpct, then merges by qtrno2 and permno.
The program reads fundturnover_ltstio and merges its short- and long-term ownership fields by quarter and permno.
The program reads IBES recommendation summaries, transforms meanrec, retains the last statpers per quarter and CUSIP, and merges by qtrno2 and CUSIP.
The program reads jointmz.earnvol with cusip, fyear and earnvol, then merges by fiscal year and CUSIP.
The program reads herdingmeasures_final2 and merges it by qtrno2 and permno.
The program reads rddata and carries rdsale by CUSIP and fiscal year; no producer appears in the supplied SAS source.
The program defines intangible from siccd and retains observations with fundturnlen, meanrec and prc at least one dollar.

evidence.quote:
This table reports average three‐day cumulative abnormal stock returns (CARs) around analyst recommendation announcements made during the past four
(left half) and next four (right half) quarters from the portfolio formation date. We separate the announcements based on whether fundamental uncertainty is
high or low. We use the following proxies: (i) earnings volatility (panel A); (ii) the ratio of R&D expenses to sales (panel B); and (iii) whether firms operate in an
“intangibles industry” (panel C). Earnings volatility is calculated as the standard deviation of deflated earnings (Income before Extraordinary Items/((Assets (t)+
Assets (t‐1))/2) over the last five fiscal years. We require a minimum of the last three years of data; otherwise earnings volatility is missing. Following
Balakrishnan, Schrand, and Vashishtha [2020], intangibles industries are SIC codes 282 (plastics and synthetic materials), 283 (drugs), 357 (computer and office
equipment), 367 (electronic components and accessories), 48 (communications), 73 (business services), 87 (engineering, accounting, R&D, and management
related services); the remaining industries are “tangible industries.” CARs are constructed as in Table 5. FUNDTURNOVER is the weighted average of the portfolio
turnover of a firm’s institutional investors (in % per quarter). MEANREC is a stock’s mean (consensus) analyst recommendation, coded on a scale from 1 (sell) to
5 (strong buy). We report results for the extreme groups only. t‐statistics are reported in parentheses. 5% significance levels are denoted in bold. Variables are
defined in the Data Appendix.
evidence.description: The supplied online appendix states a five-fiscal-year earnings-volatility window, at least three years of data, and the fundturnover and MEANREC definitions.

actions.description: Stage compatible direct inputs and resolve the missing preparation handoffs without changing the authors' formulas, filters, joins or variable definitions.
steps: Prepare the author-shaped crsp.crspdata input. CRSP.MSF is readable with CUSIP, PERMNO, DATE, PRC, RET and SHROUT, while CRSP.MSENAMES is readable with PERMNO, CUSIP, SHRCD and name-validity dates; confirm a date-valid join supplies the required share code and the author's period/product before treating the pair as compatible.

Treat catalog-listed TFN.S34 only as a 13F candidate: its label and catalog metadata identify Thomson-Reuters 13F holdings, but the bounded probe timed out and the catalog fields do not include PERMNO. Resolve readability and the time-valid CUSIP-to-PERMNO handoff before using it as Holdings.Holdings_type.

Locate compatible prepared chars, idioriskff, bushee_variables, fundturnover_ltstio, ibesrecosummary, jointmz.earnvol, herdingmeasures_final2 and rddata inputs, or obtain the omitted producer programs and their exact input/output contracts.

For chars, confirm the listed stock-quarter fields and prc consumed by the final filter; for the Bushee input, confirm year, qtr, permno, io_tra and io; for IBES, confirm CUSIP/statpers/meanrec/numrec; preserve the source's distinct year, qtrno2 and fyear keys.

Obtain the missing fundturnover_ltstio producer or exact prepared table; preserve the source comment's link to fundturnover_inst and testinst and resolve how stio_fundturn/ltio_fundturn are constructed.

COMP.FUNDA is readable with cusip, fyear, datadate, at, ib, sale and xrd columns, but the one-row probe does not establish history or nonmissing values. Obtain the omitted earnvol producer and confirm its five-fiscal-year deflated-earnings window/minimum-three rule; obtain the exact rdsale recipe and herding definitions rather than substituting guessed aliases.

The assigned frozen catalog returned no exact MEANREC/NUMREC or recsum candidate for ibesrecosummary. Confirm the author-compatible IBES recommendation-summary product and its history/identifier mapping; do not replace it with an EPS summary table.

The packaged CPS_Final Sample_Identifiers.txt is only a CUSIP/year/qtr list; it does not bypass the missing direct inputs or supply the final dataset. After staging compatible inputs, perform bounded metadata checks and later validate required keys, fields and join coverage during an authorized execution.
validation: Confirm all required source columns and key types in the staged tables.
After an authorized run, inspect merge counts and verify finaldataset contains the documented fields and passes the authored final filter.

actions.description: Resolve the actual producer handoffs and preserve the supplied SAS construction order from raw CRSP/13F inputs through the filtered finaldataset.
steps: Load quarter-end monthly CRSP and Holdings.Holdings_type; derive quarter-end rdates, sort both inputs, and merge on permno/rqdate to create the matched holdings rows. Keep the code's existing share-code/return/price filters, qtrno2/value/pctshares calculations and native SAS KEEP/RENAME behavior.

From matched holdings, form fundqtr and test2 to fill observed two-quarter reporting gaps, append test and test2 into testchange, align lagged holding values on the next qtrno2, apply maxqtr, and produce testinst. Preserve that the source's lag and semiannual logic is part of the turnover input construction.

Re-read quarter-end CRSP prices and merge with testinst; compute num/den and sum by fundno/qtrno2/semiannual into fundturnover_inst, then create lagturn1-3, the four-quarter mean and turnrank. Merge fundturnover_inst with testinst2 to create fundturnshares and aggregate to stock_fundturnover/fundturnlen.

Before the final merge, resolve the absent producer for fundturnover_ltstio. The source comment links its stio_fundturn/ltio_fundturn measures to fundturnover_inst and testinst, but no supplied block creates that table; do not consume it until the producer/schema handoff is supplied.

Merge chars with the generated stock_fundturnover by qtrno2/permno to start finaldataset. Then, in the supplied order, merge idioriskff by qtrno2/permno; bushee_variables by qtrno2/permno; fundturnover_ltstio by qtrno2/permno; IBES recommendation summary by qtrno2/CUSIP after selecting the last statpers per quarter; jointmz.earnvol by fyear/CUSIP; herdingmeasures_final2 by qtrno2/permno; and rddata by CUSIP/fyear.

Apply the supplied SIC-code intangible assignments, then retain only observations with nonmissing fundturnlen, nonmissing meanrec, and prc >= 1; persist finaldataset to the chosen durable output library. Do not infer a regression or portfolio driver from the online appendix.
validation: Before any separately authorized run, verify each producer's output dataset, keys and columns against its next consumer, including fyear versus qtrno2 and the char prc field used by the final filter.
After an authorized run, verify the documented order, the prepared-input merge keys and the persistent finaldataset output.
